clue.text: Courtly warning, of course, has bearing thus

parts.note: on a golf course the warning shout to other players is fore
N, north, is a compass bearing
sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as printed

explanation.surface: A courtier's warning issued in the right manner and bearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' points to the golf course, where FORE is the warning cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Forensic means belonging to courts of law, so courtly in the legal rather than the palace sense.

clue.text: More frequently seen in parts of Tenerife

indicators.note: the answer is seen within parts of the following words, running across their join

explanation.surface: Something is spotted more often on certain stretches of a Canary island.
explanation.definitionFit: An old comparative form meaning at shorter intervals, i.e. more often.

clue.text: One of the acts of the erstwhile common law

definitions.text: One of the acts of the erstwhile common law

parts.words: One of the acts of the erstwhile common law
parts.note: the Acts of Parliament that fenced off land formerly held in common by villagers, turning it into private fields

explanation.walkthrough: The Enclosure Acts in England turned common land into private holdings, so an enclosure is what became of the old common; 'law' plays on the legal common law.
explanation.definitionFit: Fencing off shared village land into private property was done under parliamentary acts named for this process.

clue.text: Somehow resist Solomon's spouse in the song

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of resist are rearranged in some unstated way

explanation.surface: Somehow fight off the bride of King Solomon as described in a song.
explanation.walkthrough: The Song of Solomon has the line 'my sister, my spouse', so the spouse there is called sister.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Biblical Song of Songs the lover addresses the beloved as both spouse and sibling.

clue.text: Reference made precisely at the start of the lesson

definitions.text: Reference made precisely at the start of the lesson

parts.words: Reference made precisely at the start of the lesson
parts.note: a church reading is announced by naming the exact book section and numbered line of the Bible, the model of a precise citation

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an exact citation, originally of a Biblical passage named before a reading in church.

clue.text: The fate of the clergy, love

parts.note: the cloth is a collective term for the clergy
love is nil in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: What becomes of the clergy is love.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Fates of Greek myth were Clotho, Lachesis and Atropos; Clotho spun the thread of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Clotho was one of the three Greek goddesses of destiny who spun each human life.

clue.text: Restoring a clergyman, round about four, …

indicators.note: round about says the word for the clergyman goes around the number that follows

parts.note: a curate is an assistant clergyman in a parish
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Bringing a churchman back to health takes about four of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this surface on into 7-down; 'Restoring' is the adjective sense, as in a restoring medicine, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy that brings back health is said to have healing, restorative power.

clue.text: … a cuppa stood in the garden

parts.note: cuppa is British slang for a cup of tea
rose, as in got to one's feet, means stood up

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: someone takes a cup of tea and stands up in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 6-down's surface; the definition is the loose 'in the garden', meaning something found in a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea rose is a garden shrub rose whose scent recalls tea leaves, grown in flower beds.

clue.text: How the off-beat marcher proceeds

parts.note: a soldier whose feet fall off the beat moves out of time with the rest of the column

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes someone not in rhythm with the others, literally on parade and figuratively in ideas.

clue.text: Virginia's floral supplies?

parts.note: Virginia stock is a garden flower

explanation.definitionFit: Stock is a scented garden plant, Virginia stock being one kind, and stocks are also supplies held in reserve.

clue.text: Presumptuous Agar torn and troubled

indicators.note: troubled says the letters of Agar torn are disturbed and set in a new order

explanation.surface: A presumptuous woman named Agar is torn and troubled.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone haughty and overbearing presumes too much of their own importance.

clue.text: It's idle to have a modish party with fast company

parts.note: in means fashionable, modish
a do is a British informal word for a party
Lent is the forty-day fast kept by the whole church together

explanation.surface: It is lazy to throw a trendy party with a fast-living crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast company' reads as racy friends but is the church's communal fast, Lent.
explanation.definitionFit: Lazy and averse to work, as an adjective describing the idle.

clue.text: Secret warning, but cue is useless

definitions.meaning: a private hint passed on beforehand
a cue whose leather end has come away cannot strike the ball properly

explanation.surface: A confidential warning, though the snooker cue is no good.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidential hint in advance of trouble; and a billiard cue with its leather end come away cannot be played.

clue.text: Like Lucifer — so done by a generous host ?

definitions.meaning: Lucifer, the fallen angel, was cast out for his arrogance

definitions.text: so done by a generous host

explanation.surface: Being like the Devil, so a generous host treats you?
explanation.definitionFit: Lucifer fell through pride; and a lavish host does guests well, the idiom 'done proud'.

clue.text: Divided in portions — ready for the post?

definitions.meaning: split up into shares, as land into plots
wrapped and tied as a package for mailing

explanation.surface: Split into shares and ready to be mailed.
explanation.definitionFit: Split into shares or plots; and wrapped up as a package for mailing.

clue.text: Almost all stop outside — it's widespread

indicators.note: outside says the word for stop goes around the shortened all

parts.note: to prevent something is to stop it

indicators.note: almost says the word all loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Nearly everyone halts outdoors, it's so common.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' is a link joining wordplay to definition; 'Almost' trims the last letter of 'all' before 'outside' sets the stop word around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something common and widely found everywhere is generally current.

clue.text: Wagnerian type swanning around in her long disguise

indicators.note: disguise says the letters of in her long are masked by being rearranged

explanation.surface: A Wagner character drifts about in her long disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: Wagner's knight Lohengrin arrives in a boat drawn by a swan, hence 'swanning around'.
explanation.definitionFit: The title knight of Wagner's opera travels in a boat pulled by a swan.

clue.text: Hopes may be dashed by this wretch

definitions.text: Hopes may be dashed by this
definitions.meaning: something that spoils or withers, as a disease ruins a crop

explanation.surface: This wretch may dash hopes.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a blighter is a rogue or chap; literally it is anything that blights.
explanation.definitionFit: One who spoils, as frost blights crops and dashes hopes; and British slang for a contemptible fellow.

clue.text: Cancelling the second ring

parts.note: re- is the prefix for doing something a second time
pealing is the ringing of bells

explanation.surface: Calling off the next ring of the bell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the second ring' is RE-PEALING, ringing bells again.
explanation.definitionFit: Revoking a law means withdrawing or annulling it.

clue.text: Square-based monument is highly to the point

definitions.meaning: a tomb like those at Giza, built on a square foundation
its sides climb and meet at a peak high above

explanation.surface: A square-based monument is very relevant.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt's great tombs stand on a square base; and their sides rise steeply to a single apex.

clue.text: Jack Hawker's not expensive

definitions.meaning: a ...-jack is a pedlar of low-priced wares, so the word needed precedes Jack to name a hawker

explanation.surface: Jack the street seller is not costly.
explanation.walkthrough: A cheap-jack is a travelling hawker of shoddy goods; the first sense asks for the word that turns 'Jack' into a hawker.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheap jack is a hawker of low-priced goods, so the word goes before 'Jack' to make a hawker; and it means low-priced.

clue.text: A number on the island grow together

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
Crete is the largest Greek island

explanation.surface: A count taken on a Greek island grows together.
explanation.definitionFit: To accrete is to fuse or build up by gradual accumulation.

clue.text: Occur when potatoes are lifted, for example

definitions.text: when potatoes are lifted, for example
definitions.meaning: a harvested crop is raised out of the ground

explanation.surface: It happens when potatoes are dug up, say.
explanation.definitionFit: To arise unexpectedly; and literally a harvest such as potatoes coming out of the soil.

clue.text: Get listener to rebuke the nipper

parts.note: the ear is the organ that listens
to wig is an old British word meaning to scold

explanation.surface: Have someone overhear you tell off the child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nipper' is British slang for a child, but here it is the insect with pincers at its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect has pincers at its rear and can pinch.

clue.text: Ann's booked a pass for the arena

definitions.meaning: the H.G. Wells novel Ann ... gives Ann a second name in a book
a slow sweep of the cape made by a bullfighter in the ring

explanation.surface: Ann has reserved a ticket for the stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass' suggests a ticket but is a bullfighter's cape move; 'booked' is Ann in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Ann Veronica is an H.G. Wells novel; and a slow cape movement in bullfighting.

clue.text: Fifty a minute by a boy in Cardiganshire

parts.note: L is fifty in Roman numerals
Peter is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Fifty pence a minute for a boy in a Welsh county.
explanation.walkthrough: Lampeter is a small university town in the old Welsh county of Cardiganshire, so the definition is a place found there.
explanation.definitionFit: A market and university town of mid-Wales lies within this former county.

clue.text: Dad's right to get the plaster

parts.note: pa is a child's word for father

explanation.surface: Father is entitled to fetch the sticking plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Parget is ornamental lime rendering applied to walls.

clue.text: Artful Jack Dawkins

parts.note: in Dickens's Oliver Twist the young pickpocket Jack Dawkins is known by a nickname beginning with Artful

explanation.definitionFit: Jack Dawkins is the Artful one of Oliver Twist, a nimble boy who evades capture.

clue.text: Costs of transposing the layout?

parts.note: switch the halves of the word layout to get outlay, which means money spent

explanation.definitionFit: Outlay means money paid out, so costs are spending.
